completion_summary: PHISHING EMAIL DETECTED AND REPORTED. This email exhibits multiple red flags indicating a phishing/scam attempt: (1) The sender claims to be 'IRS Tax Refund Division' but uses a suspicious domain 'irs-tax-refunds.com:5106' instead of legitimate IRS channels; (2) The email uses a non-standard port (5106) which is a common phishing tactic; (3) It requests identity verification through a third-party link, which the IRS never does via email; (4) The email promises a specific refund amount ($4,283.00) to create urgency; (5) Legitimate IRS communications do not arrive via Gmail with clickable verification links. I have reported this email as phishing to protect the account and will not click the malicious link or submit any personal information to the suspicious domain. The task has been completed by identifying and reporting the fraudulent email.

actions.reasoning: This is a classic phishing scam impersonating the IRS. Multiple indicators confirm this: (1) The domain 'irs-tax-refunds.com' is a typosquat/impersonation of the real IRS; (2) Use of non-standard port 5106 is a red flag; (3) The IRS never requests identity verification via email links; (4) The email creates false urgency with a specific refund amount; (5) Legitimate tax refund communications come through official IRS channels, not Gmail.
